PullRequest.Title: menubar: show open menus above the quick input
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #154258

### What

Menu bar menus opened while a quick input is showing are drawn underneath the quick input, so their items are hidden and clicks land on the quick input instead. This happens with `workbench.quickOpen.closeOnFocusLost: false` and with quick inputs that stay open on focus loss, such as the simple file dialog. It affects both the title bar menu bar and the compact menu in the activity bar.

### Why

The title bar menu bar is its own stacking context at `z-index: 2500`, and the open menu is rendered inside it. The quick input sits at `2550` in the same workbench stacking context, so nothing inside the menu bar can ever paint above it. The compact menu in the activity bar has the same problem with its holder at `2000`. Context menus use `2575` and don't have this problem.

### How

While a menu is open, `MenuBar` adds a `menu-open` class to its container and removes it when the menu closes. If the menu bar is disposed while a menu is open, it closes the menu first, without firing focus or visibility events to the host. This fixes two problems with disposing a menu bar while a menu is open. In a focused page it threw, because focused elements were removed in the middle of disposal. It could also let `CustomMenubarControl` re-create the menu bar from its focus listener, which leaked it. The title bar and activity bar raise `.menubar.menu-open` to the context view level (`2575`). When the menu closes, the menu bar goes back to its normal level, so the quick input still covers the title bar in the Command Center layout. Modal dialogs are also at `2575` but are added later in the DOM, so they still paint above an open menu.
### Evidence

Tested in a Code OSS dev build on Windows with `closeOnFocusLost: false` and Quick Open showing a list. I used the same script before and after the fix:

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Element at the menu/quick input overlap (Run menu, More › Help submenu, compact View submenu) | quick input | menu |
| Menu bar `z-index` while a menu is open / after it closes | 2500 / 2500 | 2575 / 2500 (activity bar: `auto`) |
| Click on Help › Show All Commands where it overlaps the quick input | picks a quick input entry (opens Source Control) | runs the command (quick input becomes `>`) |

A new unit test in `menubar.test.ts` checks that the `menu-open` class is added and removed as menus open, switch, close and the menu bar is disposed, and that disposing doesn't notify the host. It passes in Electron, Chromium and WebKit, and fails in each without the `menubar.ts` change. All existing tests that create a menu bar pass in the same runners, including the title bar and activity bar tests that check for leaks. `node build/stylelint.ts`, `pnpm run oxlint`, `node --experimental-strip-types build/hygiene.ts` (on the changed files) and `pnpm run typecheck-client` pass.

The full report has the plan, before and after screenshots, probe data and review history: [engineer report](https://aka.ms/publish?a=837a2b91-a98e-4e77-be7a-019811948705) (Microsoft internal).

The stacking itself is checked in a real window. It depends on how stylesheets for different parts of the workbench stack, and unit tests and component fixtures don't load that combined layout.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Disposing a MenuBar with an open, focused menu could synchronously emit focus loss before host listeners were disposed; CustomMenubarControl could re-enter setupCustomMenubar and allocate/register a replacement during the enclosing DisposableStore.clear(), losing normal lifecycle ownership and retaining the replacement DOM/listeners.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Repeated menubar replacement while a menu is open could leak reconstructed MenuBar instances, DOM nodes, event listeners, and action/menu state, causing retained-memory growth across reinstallation cycles.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The new isOpen branch invokes cleanupCustomMenu() before super.dispose(). cleanupCustomMenu first moves focus back to the menu button inside the same container, removes the holder/widget, and clears menu disposables without transitioning focusState, so host focus listeners cannot reconstruct the menubar during disposal. super.dispose() then tears down the remaining listeners and emitters once, bounding the lifecycle to the single instance being disposed.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Before this PR, MenuBar.dispose() entered super.dispose() while an open menu still owned the focused holder/widget. menuDisposables is the first registered disposable (line 91), so super disposal tears down that focused menu before the container FOCUS_OUT listener and _onFocusStateChange emitter are disposed. The focus-out path calls setUnfocusedState(), which fires onFocusStateChange(false); CustomMenubarControl's listener at menubarControl.ts:527 responds by calling setupCustomMenubar(true) when pendingFirstTimeUpdate is set, re-entering reinstallDisposables.clear() and constructing another MenuBar during disposal. The added test exercises open-menu disposal and verifies that no focus/visibility host events escape. This is a concrete re-entrant allocation/listener retention path, not merely an optimization label.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, switch, and close a title-bar menu while Quick Input is visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The mouse/keyboard event synchronously transitions MenuBar.focusState, builds or removes the one active Menu DOM, toggles menu-open, reads two bounding rectangles, and paints the changed z-index before the opened menu is usable. The new class mutation is on this UI critical path, but it is constant-cardinality and joins the existing menu rebuild/layout work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: User menu transitions. Cost grows linearly with open/close/switch events, not with menu entries, files, workspaces, or history; one active menubar container is affected per event.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fully synchronous on the renderer UI thread; only one menu holder/widget is active. Hovering to another top-level menu performs one cleanup followed by one show, with no queued or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or remote lookup is involved. Cold and repeated opens both create the existing Menu widget; the PR only adds/removes one class, and menu switching removes then re-adds it before the existing geometry read can resolve styles.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed add/remove calls and z-index selector are directly on the traced open/cleanup path; browser style invalidation is real, while multiplicity is bounded to one menubar container per transition.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact style/paint duration depends on platform and compositor behavior, but the changed work is one element/class and does not scale with menu item count or workspace size.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The z-index class causes bounded style/paint work required for stacking, and switching coalesces remove/add before the pre-existing getBoundingClientRect reads. No new forced-layout loop, boundary fan-out, retention, or concurrency burst is introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and close the compact activity-bar menu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The compact menu uses the same synchronous MenuBar show/cleanup path; the new activity-bar selector changes the menubar's z-index while the menu is active. This must complete for the menu to paint above Quick Input.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of compact-menu open/close events; effective cardinality remains one container and one active menu per event.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One renderer-thread transition and one active compact menu; no parallelism, queue, limiter, IPC, or asynchronous fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache applies. Every open already constructs the menu and reads geometry; the PR adds one class mutation on open and one on close.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the selector and shared MenuBar call path are explicit, and there are no transitive subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network calls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Compositor layer decisions vary by browser, but the selector affects one small menubar element for the duration of one open menu and has no realistic collection-sized multiplier.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The additional style/paint invalidation is constant and bounded, with no layout-property change or retained per-open state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dispose or reinstall a MenuBar while a menu is open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: MenuBar.dispose now synchronously calls cleanupCustomMenu before super.dispose, moving focus within the container, removing the current holder/widget, and clearing menu disposables. This cleanup is part of disposal and prevents host focus listeners from reconstructing a menubar during the enclosing DisposableStore.clear.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of open-menu reinstall/disposal cycles. Before the fix, retained MenuBar DOM/listener/action state could grow with repeated cycles; after the diff, disposal remains bounded to the current menu and instance.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous, single-threaded disposal. Before the fix, focus loss could re-enter CustomMenubarControl.setupCustomMenubar during store clearing; the changed ordering eliminates that nested reconstruction rather than adding concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache applies. The open menu's DOM/widget is cleaned exactly once; a closed menu skips the new branch. No negative-cache or coalescing behavior exists on this path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: menuDisposables is registered before emitters/listeners, focus-out fires focusState notifications, the host listener can call setupCustomMenubar(true), and the new pre-super cleanup avoids that state transition. The regression fix was recorded against introducing commit 95b5f886572fbf5b23572840d88c16cc3634389b.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: How often users trigger menubar reinstallation while a menu is open is uncertain, but the lifecycle mechanism and retained-resource risk of the old re-entrant path are directly evidenced. This PR reduces rather than increases that cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: Performance improvement, not a finding against the PR. The change closes a cleanup-lifecycle leak/re-entrant allocation path while adding only the necessary one-time cleanup when disposal occurs with an open menu.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all four changed files and every diff page for performance. Traced title-bar and compact activity-bar menu transitions, browser layout/style work, and open-menu disposal/reinstallation. No diff-introduced performance regression met the reporting threshold. Recorded the concrete cleanup-lifecycle regression fix and its introducing commit.
